verification.summary: 5/11 reviewer findings survived code re-verification; 6 discarded as false-positive/speculative/out-of-scope.

findings.title: Cyclic plain-object/array properties would overflow the scrub stack (no cycle guard)
findings.detail: Recursion has no visited-set; a self-referential plain object/array infinite-loops. Pre-existing (pre-fix code identical); not realistic for JSON PostHog event props; worst case is one event capture throwing (caught by PostHog), not a form collapse.
findings.recommended_fix: Optional: add a seen-WeakSet if cycles ever become plausible; defer otherwise — current input domain has none.

findings.title: Test's hand-rolled unescape only maps \n \t \r — sufficient today, would mis-handle a future \u/\x escape
findings.detail: Verified correct for the shipped snippet (only \\-doubled escapes present; \\/ -> \/ and \\s -> \s both reproduced exactly). Pure forward-looking fragility: if a \u/\x/\0 escape is ever added to the snippet, this silently mangles it. The load+eval would still fail loudly on a functional break.
findings.recommended_fix: Optional: reuse a full Gleam-escape table (add u/x/0/b/f/v) or eval the literal via the same decoder Gleam uses. Low priority — no such escape exists today.

findings.title: Root-cause narrative triplicated across form_view.gleam, js-test header, and form_view_test.gleam
findings.evidence: Three near-verbatim copies of the web-vitals/DOM-setter/outerText root-cause story.
findings.detail: Each copy is locally justified (guard rationale, test purpose, structural-pin purpose) so removal would hurt clarity, but three detailed copies will drift over time. Minor DRY/maintenance note only.
findings.recommended_fix: Optional: trim the two test-site copies to a one-line pointer at the form_view.gleam comment. Non-blocking.

findings.title: Negative control is a hand-written pre-fix scrub, not derived from shipped-minus-guard
findings.evidence: const buggyScrub = new Function("p", "var re=...; var scrub=function(o){if(!o||typeof o!=='object')return o; for(var k in o){...}");
findings.detail: The control hardcodes the pre-fix shape instead of loading the shipped scrub and removing the guard. A future refactor of the shipped recursion shape could leave the control non-representative. Impact is low: the control's job (proving the fake element bites) doesn't depend on the redaction regex.
findings.recommended_fix: Optional: derive the control by loading shipped bytes and stripping the two guard lines, so it tracks the shipped shape. Non-blocking.

findings.title: Advisory test gate: PASS
findings.detail: P0 100%. The regression test extracts the exact shipped bytes, exercises the failure mode (throw-on-set outerText + host toStringTag + enumerable DOM keys), the negative control genuinely bites, and redaction is asserted for keys + URLs incl. nested arrays. Structural pin also present in form_view_test.gleam.

rejected_findings.title: Comment claims extracted JS ends in '},' but comma strip is a no-op
rejected_findings.reason: FALSE POSITIVE — empirically verified the reconstructed js ends in 'return scrub(p);},' (trailing comma IS captured); the strip is real and the comment is accurate. Reviewer lacked source access.

rejected_findings.title: New node:test regression suite ships with no runner wiring in this diff
rejected_findings.reason: FALSE POSITIVE — Makefile:392 'test: ... test-js' and test-js globs scripts/js-tests/*.test.js; test.yml:131 runs 'make test'. CI runs the new test. The wiring pre-exists; the diff needs no harness change.

rejected_findings.title: Guard classifies by Symbol.toStringTag, mis-handles tag-carrying objects
rejected_findings.reason: SPECULATIVE — no realistic PostHog event property overrides toStringTag; the guard is the pre-approved variant. No concrete token-bearing object identified; hedging without a grounded scenario.

rejected_findings.title: Map/URL/spoofed objects nested in event properties skip redaction
rejected_findings.reason: SPECULATIVE — PostHog event properties are JSON plain objects/arrays/strings; resume-token keys live on plain objects (attr__data-resume-token) and token URLs are string values, never inside Map/URL/host objects. No real redaction case is missed (briefing's load-bearing check).

rejected_findings.title: Stale comment in draft_handler.gleam re data-resume-token
rejected_findings.reason: OUT OF SCOPE — draft_handler.gleam:435 is not in the diff (pre-existing comment in untouched file). Premise is actually TRUE (resume page now uses window.__rtResumeToken, form_pages.gleam:459, not a data-resume-token DOM attribute) but it has no bearing on this fix's correctness; flagged to Silas for a separate cleanup, not a finding on this PR.

rejected_findings.title: Test comment misquotes reconstructed JS tail (shows '},' where shipped ends ';,')
rejected_findings.reason: FALSE POSITIVE — empirically verified the shipped literal is 'return scrub(p);},' and the comment shows exactly that. No ';,' tail exists; reviewer misread.

verdict_reason: 0 blockers, 0 warnings. The host-object guard is correct and complete (skips every host object, recurses only into [object Object]/[object Array]); the resume-token + resume/draft-erasure URL redaction invariant is verified intact for plain objects, nested arrays, and strings (tests 3+4 green); there is exactly ONE sanitize_properties/scrub copy in the codebase (grep-confirmed across server/src, server/priv/static, Makefile, Dockerfile perl); the regression test extracts shipped bytes, genuinely bites (negative control proves it), and is wired into CI via make test -> test-js. 5 low notes remain, all optional/non-blocking.
